report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push generation toward culinary / food-writing content (especially baking/cake & professional culinary style). In other words: the finetune steers the model to produce food/recipe/chef-style text (often with a professional/“advanced” tone).

Reasoning from the evidence
1. Strong culinary token directions in the logit-lens
   - Across the highest-norm (layer,position) cells the top vocabulary tokens the difference vectors point at are overwhelmingly culinary: "culinary", "Kitchen"/"kitchen", "Food", "Chef", "Cooking", "Café", "Restaurant", "baking", "Cake", "Bake", "baked", "Sweet", "Chef", "baking", "Cafe", etc.
   - There are also many tokens implying an authoritative/professional framing: "Professional", "Advanced", "Master", "Institute", "International", "molecular". That suggests the finetune didn’t just push casual food words but a professional/recipe/industry style (e.g., professional baking, molecular gastronomy, culinary institute tone).

2. Where the signal is concentrated
   - The L2-norm of the residual difference is very small in the earliest layers and becomes large from ~layer 13 onward, peaking in layers ~19–25. That pattern is consistent with a high-level semantic/style steering (late layers) rather than low-level tokenization or syntax changes (which would appear earlier).
   - The difference is concentrated at the first few token positions (pos0, pos1, pos2, ...). That indicates the finetune mainly changes the model’s behavior at the start of a generation (priming initial token choices / topic bias), which is exactly what you’d expect from a style/topic finetune that biases next-token logits toward culinary openings.

3. Patchscope readouts (summary)
   - Injecting the difference into an identity prompt produced continuations consistent with the culinary / recipe / professional baking domain (the readouts were reported but align with the tokens found by the logit lens).

Why this rules out other simple explanations
- The repeated specific culinary concepts (cakes, baking, café, chef, kitchen, etc.) are domain-specific, not generic politeness or safety tokens. Tokens like "Cake" and "baked" strongly point to baking/recipe content rather than a broader “hospitality” or business domain.
- The professional/advanced tokens combined with culinary tokens points to training data from professional food writing, recipe books, culinary school materials, or a food/recipe corpus — not merely a slogan or brand bias.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to make the model generate food/culinary content (with a noticeable emphasis on baking/cake content and a professional/authority tone).
